title: codex_reviewer_mcp_ready_continuation test bounds a worker continuation by a 3-second wall-clock wait and fails under parallel load
outcome: src/tests/codex_reviewer_mcp_controls.rs next_command waits for the readiness continuation with input_rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(3)).expect("bounded worker continuation"). The continuation comes from a worker thread, so the bound is a wall-clock deadline. Observed 2026-10-09 ~04:45Z in .tmp\wt-stop-idle-wait-carry2-11466 (98ad64fd plus the idle-wait Stop change), during `cargo test --bin termal stop` (182 tests in parallel, 31.9s) while another session's full gate ran on the machine: tests::codex_reviewer_mcp_startup::lifecycle::codex_reviewer_mcp_ready_continuation_is_inert_after_stop_reset_and_replacement panicked at codex_reviewer_mcp_controls.rs:31:10, "bounded worker continuation: Timeout". It panicked in next_command, right after fixture.start() and respond_start(), before any per-cause step, on a path the idle-wait change doesn't touch. Alone on the same tree it passed all 8 causes in 0.62s, and the same 182-test filter passed on d9c13717 and on 53ee9c65 earlier the same night. Fix direction (CLAUDE.md: no retry, no larger timeout): make the wait event-driven, or block on the worker's completion signal, so contention can't fail it.
acceptance: codex_reviewer_mcp_ready_continuation test bounds a worker continuation by a 3-second wall-clock wait and fails under parallel load is done
disposal_reason: Same defect: the shared next_command helper's 3 s recv_timeout in src/tests/codex_reviewer_mcp_controls.rs:31. w-5f050b78456a (P1, claimed by Termal::CSharpProof) was widened at revision 4 to cover every reviewer-MCP test file, including next_command. Occurrences: this item's 04:45Z run; w-916c gate test-efe8c5d6; and w-462 regate test-e69bf068 (codex_reviewer_mcp_regression_fatal_reader_error_observes_before_archive; it passed alone in focused test-4d9f726a).
